FCC Decision Allows Your Online Activity to Continue Being Tracked

This is concerning the FCC's decision to allow websites to ignore DNT requests, I assume?

If so, that headline is so, so wrong. If the FCC were to force websites to adhere to DNT requests, then it would require every single website that does any kind of tracking (As in, remembering that you're logged into a site so you don't have to log in every single time, remembering preferences, knowing your location [which is bad but obviously has some benefits that don't outweigh how bad it is], etc etc) to cater to you, and to change how it functions based on a packet your computer sends it. Although in a perfect world this would be nice, websites should be static, and shouldn't generally be expected to cater to anyone in a way that wasn't hard coded into a website.

tl;dr expecting to be able to tick a checkbox in your browser and have the servers of websites you visit function differently ~just for you~ is retarded and you should have your own privacy measures in place anyways

There is a huge difference between keeping track of settings, and keeping track of your activity. If the FCC had decided in favor of privacy, then sites would still be able to use methods (cookies, localStorage, db, etc) to keep preferences and settings, they just wouldn't be allowed to track your activity and merge it with the rest of "big data" to profile a user.

This is a huge disappointment for internet privacy and security advocates.

Just switch to Firefox, it has built-in tracking prevention in Private mode now.

Go to about:config and switch privacy.trackingprotection.enabled to true, and then you don't even need to use a private browsing window.
